_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 31 (Jacob flees Laban; mizpah covenant). Saadia-specific: v.13 'אלטאיק אלמבשרך' = 'the Power who appeared/gave good tidings to you in Beth-El' (consistent w/ Sufficient-Power name elsewhere; Saadia adds 'who appeared/announced'); v.19 'אלתמת'אל' = 'the image/figurine' (Saadia uses singular form for teraphim — perhaps a household idol); v.30 'מעבודי' = 'my objects of worship' (concrete substitute for 'אלהי'); v.42 'פזע יצחק' = 'the Fear of Isaac' (kept as a proper attribute-name); v.47 'רגם אלשהאדה' = 'the Cairn of Witness' (rendering יגר שהדותא Aramaically — Saadia translates the name's meaning); v.49 'המטלע' = 'the Watcher' for המצפה.

translations.1: And he heard the words of Laban's sons, saying: 'Jacob has taken all that belongs to our father; and from what was our father's he has acquired all this wealth.'
translations.2: And Jacob saw the face of Laban — and behold, it was not with him as before.
translations.3: Then God said to Jacob: 'Return to the land of your fathers and your birthplace; and I shall be with you.'
translations.4: And Jacob sent and called for Rachel and Leah, to the wilderness, to his flock.
translations.5: And he said to them: 'Behold, I see the face of your father — that it is not with me as before. But the God of my father has never ceased to be with me.
translations.6: And you know that I have served him with all my strength.
translations.7: And your father has dealt deceitfully with me, and changed my wage ten times; but God did not let him do me harm.
translations.8: If he said, 'Thus shall be your wage — the speckled ones,' all the flock bore speckled. And if he said, 'Thus shall be your wage — the striped,' all the flock bore striped.
translations.9: So God has bestowed of your father's flock, and given to me.
translations.10: And it was at the time when the flock was in heat — I lifted up my eyes, and saw in a dream — and behold, the male goats mounting the flock were striped, and speckled, and dappled.
translations.11: And the angel of God said to me in the dream: 'O Jacob.' I said: 'I am at your service.'
translations.12: He said: 'Lift up your eyes and look — all the male goats mounting the flock are striped, and speckled, and dappled — for I have seen all that Laban has been doing to you.
translations.13: I am the Power who appeared to you in Beth-El, where you anointed for Me the pillar, and vowed to Me there the vow. Now arise, go out from this land, and return to the land of your birth.'
translations.14: And Rachel and Leah answered, and said to him: 'Have we any portion or inheritance left in our father's house?
translations.15: Are we not reckoned by him as strangers? For he has sold us, and even consumed our price.
translations.16: All the wealth which God has bestowed from our father — it is ours and our children's. Now, whatever God has said to you, do.'
translations.17: Then Jacob arose, and lifted his sons and his wives upon the camels.
translations.18: And he drove all his livestock, and all his possessions which he had acquired — with his livestock and the rest of his property which he had acquired in Paddan-Aram — to come to Isaac his father, to the land of Canaan.
translations.19: And Laban had gone to shear his sheep; and Rachel took the image-figurine which belonged to her father.
translations.20: And Jacob concealed [his plan] from Laban the Aramean — he did not tell him that he was leaving.
translations.21: And he departed, he and all his property; and he arose, and crossed the Euphrates; and he set his course for Mount Gilead.
translations.22: And on the third day Laban was told that Jacob had fled.
translations.23: And he took his kinsmen with him, and pursued after him a journey of seven days; and he overtook him at Mount Gilead.
translations.24: And the angel of God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream of the night; and he said to him: 'Beware lest you speak to Jacob from good to evil.'
translations.25: And Laban overtook Jacob; and Jacob had pitched his tent on the mountain; and Laban encamped his kinsmen on Mount Gilead.
translations.26: And Laban said to Jacob: 'What is this you have done to me — that you concealed it from me, and led my daughters away like captives of the sword?
translations.27: Why did you hide and depart, and concealed it from me, and did not tell me — that I might have escorted you with joy and song, with timbrels and lutes?
translations.28: And you did not let me kiss my sons and my daughters. Now, you have acted foolishly in what you have done.
translations.29: Is there strength in my hand to do you harm? But the God of your father last night said to me: 'Beware lest you speak to Jacob from good to evil.'
translations.30: And now, you have gone — for you longed for your father's house. But why did you steal my objects of worship?'
translations.31: And Jacob answered him, and said: 'Because I was afraid, and said: lest you should take your daughters from me by force.
translations.32: And whoever you find your worshipped-objects with — let him not live. In the presence of our kinsmen identify whatever you have of yours with me, and take it.' And Jacob did not know that Rachel had hidden them.
translations.33: And Laban entered Jacob's tent, and Leah's tent, and the tents of the two maidservants, and he found nothing. Then he came out from Leah's tent, and entered Rachel's tent.
translations.34: And she had taken the image-figurine and placed it in the camel's saddle, and sat upon it. And Laban felt all over the tent, and did not find anything.
translations.35: And she said to him: 'Let it not press upon my lord — for I cannot rise from before you, since the way of women has come upon me.' And he searched, and did not find the image-figurine.
translations.36: And it grew hard upon Jacob; and he quarreled with him, and answered, and said: 'What is my crime? What is my offense? — that you have pursued me?
translations.37: And you have felt all my vessels; what have you found of all the vessels of your house? Set it here, before my kinsmen and your kinsmen, that they may judge between the two of us.
translations.38: Behold, twenty years have I been with you; your ewes and your she-goats have not miscarried; and the rams of your flock I have not eaten.
translations.39: A torn beast — I did not bring it to you; from my own hand you would demand it; whatever was stolen by day or by night, you would demand.
translations.41: Behold, twenty years have I been in your house: I served you fourteen years for your two daughters, and six years for your flocks; and you changed my wage ten times.
translations.42: Had not the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the Fear of Isaac, been my helper, by now you would have sent me away empty. My weakness and the toil of my hands — God saw, and reproved you last night.'
translations.43: And Laban answered him, and said to him: 'The daughters are my daughters, and the children are my children, and the flock is my flock; and all that you see is mine. And what would I do this day to my daughters, or to their children whom they have borne?
translations.44: Now come, let us make a covenant — I and you; and let it be a witness between me and you.'
translations.45: And Jacob took a stone, and set it up as a pillar.
translations.46: And Jacob said to his kinsmen: 'Gather stones.' And they gathered stones, and made a cairn; and they ate there upon the cairn.
translations.47: And Laban named it Cairn-of-Witness (Yegar-Sahaduta); and Jacob named it in Hebrew, Gal-Ed.
translations.48: And Laban said: 'This cairn is witness between me and you this day.' Therefore he named it Gal-Ed.
translations.49: And [it is also called] the Watcher — for he said: 'May God watch between me and you, when we are concealed each one from his fellow:
translations.50: that you shall not afflict my daughters, and shall not take wives in addition to them; no human stranger is with us; look — God is witness between me and you.'
translations.51: And he said to him also: 'Behold this cairn and this pillar, which I have set up between me and you.
translations.52: This cairn is witness, and the pillar — that I shall not pass over them to you, and that you shall not pass over them to me — for evil.
translations.53: May the God of Abraham, and the God of Nahor — judge between us — the God of their father.' And Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.
translations.54: And Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mountain, and called his kinsmen to eat bread; and they ate bread, and lodged on the mountain.
